thread:
Ana (ML infra): Quick question — for the SLO tuning work are we leaning toward real traffic replay or synthetic load for p95/p99 measurements? We need to capture KV cache warm-up behavior and microbatch sizing effects. Thoughts?
Devon: Real replay gives fidelity but raises privacy/storage ops. Synthetic lets us hit adversarial tails. I vote hybrid.
Samir: Hybrid + varied arrival models. Poisson for normal load, heavy-tailed (Pareto) for bursts/tails. Also exercise different seq lengths.
Samir: Example synthetic runner we used:
```
# synth load mix (poisson + bursts)
go-runner --rps=400 --burst=200 --dist=pareto --seed=42 --kv-warm=5000\```
Jules: Microbatch sizing is a big lever. Quick numbers from an old run: bs=1 p99=220ms, bs=4 p99=120ms, bs=8 p99=480ms. So larger microbatches can blow up tail due to batching waits.
Kait: Profiling points to kernel fallback + KV merge stalls causing tails. nvprof/log snippet:
```
[GPU] kernel_selector.cpp: fallback_kernel() + attention_kv_merge
timings: conv_attn_fwd: 14ms, attention_kv_merge: 98ms\```
Ana (ML infra): So action item: measure cold vs warm KV cache explicitly. My proposal: replay anonymized request shapes for fidelity (no payloads), and run synthetic adversarial bursts to stress tails. We should also log kernel choice per request. :thumbsup:
Devon: Agreed. Keep payloads out, store only shapes/timings + kv_hit bool. That keeps replayable traces without PII. :lock:
Samir: On SLO calculation: use p99 over 5-min rolling windows for alerting, but also track p95 of the heavy-shape cohort (requests whose compute >90th percentile). Otherwise regressions hide in aggregates. :thinking:
replay-bot: replay completed: 12k requests, avg_rps=320, kv_warm_ratio=0.63
Jules: From this replay model-A picks int8 kernel ~80% but falls back to fp16 on long sequences -> huge tail. We should expose kernel_id + fallback_reason in traces. :eyes:
Kait: I'll add kernel_id and kv_hit boolean to the trace schema and emit microbatch_size histogram per second so we can separate waiting vs execution latency. :rocket:
Ana (ML infra): Decision: hybrid benchmark approach. Tasks: (1) Weekend replay of anonymized shapes (Jules) (2) Synthetic burst suite for tails (Samir) (3) Add kernel & KV fields + microbatch_size histogram to traces (Kait). Aim: consolidated results by Tue. :calendar:
Devon: Note — run burst tests on dedicated capacity to avoid autoscaler noise. Flagging as a precondition. :warning:
Samir: Draft SLO suggestion for discussion: "SLO: 95% <= 120ms, 99% <= 250ms measured over 5-min windows; target microbatch <=4; rollback if p99 > 300ms sustained for 10m." Feedback?
Jules: Per-model SLOs probably necessary — long-seq models won't hit those global numbers. We should baseline per-model and have global fallback routing policy. :+1:
Ana (ML infra): Agreed. We'll baseline per-model and surface regressions per model. I'll open a doc in #docs with the methodology and attach the replay command + sample traces. Closing thread for now. :white_check_mark:
